Dmitri: Heads-up — I'm seeing a regression in prefix/prompt-cache latency after the compact-allocator flip that landed yesterday on prod-gpu-4. p99 token latency up ~12% for long prompts (>1024). No hard OOMs reported but workspace peaks spiked.

Taylor: Thanks. Do you have the profiler traces or a quick repro? Is this steady or only under certain batching patterns?

Dmitri: Repro is kind of stable on mid-tail traffic. p50 unchanged, p95 +3%, p99 +12%. This looks correlated with larger workspace allocations during kernel selection for some attention kernels. No immediate OOM alerts but infra spikes.

perf-bot: Automatic trace summary (trace id: trace-1956-03-17):
```
kernel_select: attention_v2_fused -> fallback_large_ws
workspace_peak: 12.1GB (+3.4GB vs baseline)
kvcache_alloc: 3.2GB
continuous_batching: average batch_size=8
cpu/worker: no stalls
regression_likelihood: high
```

Sasha: My read: compact allocator reduced free-list fragmentation but also made small buffer reuse slightly less predictable. Kernel selector sees less contiguous free workspace and chooses the "large_ws" codepath as it's conservative. The large_ws path has higher latency and alloc churn. See my comment on the selector PR: https://repo/commit/ab12c3f.

Katie: I ran the trace locally with a simple sim that toggles shard TTL and shard count. Command: 
```
python tools/sim_prefixcache.py --trace traces/1956-03-17.json --compact-alloc=true --shards 128 --ttl 3600
```
Output (summary):
shards=128 ttl=3600 => mem=56GB hitrate=0.87 p99_add=+12%
shards=64  ttl=1800 => mem=42GB hitrate=0.83 p99_add=+4%
shards=32  ttl=900  => mem=28GB hitrate=0.75 p99_add=+1%

Katie: So we can trade memory for latency: fewer shards + lower TTL shrinks memory and reduces the frequency of the large-ws selection because KV footprint is smaller and allocator has more contiguous space. But hitrate drops — need to check quality impact for our top prompt sets.

Dmitri: Useful numbers. My proposed experiment plan:
1) Canary revert: rollback compact-alloc for only prefixcache on prod-gpu-4 (10% traffic) for 2h. Measure p99, workspace_peak, KV hitrate.
2) Simultaneous config test: reduce prefixcache shards 128->64 and TTL 3600->1800 on a canary pool (10%). Monitor hitrate and latency.
3) If rollback helps, rework allocator to expose contiguous reservation at kvcache allocation time (avoid global compaction during active kernel select).

Dmitri: Also consider a defensive change in kernel selector to prefer small-ws kernels when workspace delta < 1MB and p99 risk is high. That would be a short mitigation.

Taylor: Sounds good. For canary metrics set alerts: p99 token latency +6% as warning, +10% as critical. Workspace_peak increase >2GB critical. KV hitrate drop >6% warning. I'll add dashboards.

Sasha: I can prototype a selector patch that adds a tie-breaker for small-ws preference. If we do that, might avoid full allocator revert. Will need microbenchmarks: selector unit tests + 1k-run perf harness.

infra-bot: Created ticket INF-3212: "prefixcache: compact-alloc -> workspace regression investigation" — https://tickets/INF-3212. Assigned: Dmitri, Sasha. Canary pool created: prod-gpu-4-canary-1 (10%).

Dmitri: Thanks. I'll start the rollback canary and run Katie's sim variants in parallel. ETA 2–3 hours for first data.

Katie: I'll generate a short eval comparing hitrate quality on our regression prompt set (regset-v1) for shards=64/TTL=1800 and report drift.

Taylor: If canary looks good after 2h we can decide whether to keep selector patch + shard config or fully revert.

Dmitri: Agreed. Keeping notes here for postmortem. cc @perf-bot for follow-up alerts. :thumbsup:
